items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: And I went to work on this job with a boy named Crump. He was a drummer. ... To make a long story short, we played that job.

ctx.x: And I made $5.00. It was a matinee dance in 1924. I shall never forget it as long as I live. And that gave me a little inspiration. And the next job I took, I took a job at a place called Fairman's, which is about six miles outside of town.

And I went to work on this job with a boy named Crump. He was a drummer. And I forget who played the piano, it's been so long ago. And I tried to tune up with the piano and didn't know how to tune up.

To make a long story short, we played that job. And it was on a Saturday night -- I shall never forget it. And back in those days, most every car you rode in was a touring car. So, on my way back home I got in the car -- I was supposed to ride back -- ride back to North Little Rock. And I set up in the car and went to sleep. I had my horn in my lap, and my arm around it. But I had a watch that I had bought. And it was an Elgin watch with a chain on it. And I went to sleep. And when I got home and got out of the…
